You're absolutely right, thank you for the correction. 

`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is 2^53 - 1 (9007199254740991). This is the largest integer where you can safely represent all integers up to that point with guaranteed uniqueness.

While 2^53 itself (9007199254740992) can be represented in JavaScript, it's where the collision problem begins—both 2^53 and 2^53 + 1 round to the same floating-point value due to the precision limits of IEEE 754 double-precision format. So 2^53 - 1 is the practical limit for working with integers where you can be certain each integer value is distinct.
